text: Mexico nabs notorious drug cartel leader. Mexico’s military captured an alleged drug lord listed among the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, sparking violent exchanges of gunfire in Sinaloa state on Friday that sent fans fleeing from a baseball game. According to *CNN*, Mexico’s defence ministry said Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” who leads the Sinaloa-based cartel Los Mazatlecos, was arrested with the help of the US. *CNN* has approached US authorities for comment. The operation was conducted by “elite military forces” using “stealth and surprise” to reach their target, the ministry posted on *X*, saying Meza-Flores was taken to Mexico City following his arrest. Two other alleged members of the criminal organisation were arrested in the same operation, Mexico’s Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said in a post on *X*. They include the group’s second-in-command, Germán “N,” alias “Serafín,” and José “N,” its alleged financial operator. Meza-Flores is “allegedly responsible for the possession, distribution, and importation of large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States,” according to an FBI wanted poster offering a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest. He was previously indicted in 2019 for drug trafficking violations and possession of a firearm, and in 2012 for drug trafficking charges, it said. The US Drug Enforcement Administration called the arrest a “significant blow” to a violent criminal organisation and praised intelligence sharing between the two countries. “(The) DEA commends the Mexican authorities who carried out this operation,” the agency said in a statement to *CNN*. In a 2013 statement, the US Treasury Department said the Meza-Flores cartel had been involved in “an extremely violent turf war” with the rival Sinaloa Cartel – then led by notorious drug lord Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, who is now serving time in a US prison. The operation to capture Meza-Flores sparked violent clashes on Friday between the Mexican military and armed militants in Guasave, an area known as the agricultural heart of Mexico. The defence ministry said that authorities “came under attack with gunfire and explosives” upon initiating the operation, and that militants set up roadblocks in several municipalities near the arrest site. Dramatic footage, verified by CNN, shows a barrage of rapid fire from what appear to be Mexican security force helicopters firing at the ground and circling over Guasave city. Video captured by a surveillance camera shows an apparent exchange of gunfire between cartel members in the back of a truck and Mexican security force helicopters above in the city of Guasave in Mexico on Friday night.
